executive_assessment.text: Southern Madagascar's panel evidence links drought-period livelihood stress with perceived violence and last-resort migration, subject to perception and attribution limits.
Named southern regions have reported restoration outputs; east-coast cyclone evidence adds differentiated service and protection vulnerabilities, with agency outputs distinguished from impact.
Post-Gezani displacement-site crowding and limited services heightened child violence/exploitation risk; incidence changes were not measured.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2025-06-02 reports: By June 2025, the World Bank reported MIONJO served about 1.4 million people in 235 rural communes across Atsimo-Andrefana, Androy and Anosy; project partners had stabilized 1,500 hectares of dunes, reforested 330 hectares and established 24 nurseries.

known_gaps.text: The NDC's 2026 figures are summarized in French, and the opened Grand Sud CCDR passage does not isolate climate's contribution to violence; no country-specific causal estimate of climate effects on conflict was opened.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
The Grand Sud fragility statement is contextual, not a complete climate-conflict mechanism.
A disaster displacement count is exposure evidence, without violent-conflict or anthropogenic event attribution.
OCHA's Global Humanitarian Overview 2022 PDF returned 403; indexed text was excluded, leaving an evidence gap on insecurity and humanitarian access during drought.
The World Bank drought-monitoring article summarizes respondent perceptions and reported social trends, not official violence rates or causal estimates; its drought period was 2018-2022.
The HCT note's January 2026 food-insecurity forecast is historical by the October 2026 access date; no subsequent measured outcome was reviewed.
The HCT note does not enumerate all 22 affected districts, and the reviewed sources do not demonstrate FCV preventing implementation of a specific climate-adaptation intervention.
MIONJO feature and UNICEF cyclone story are agency-reported results; no independent project impact evaluation was reviewed for the reported outputs.
The panel summary supports source-stated livelihood-stress/violence mechanisms but not a causal effect estimate. Protection concerns after Gezani are not incident counts.
The humanitarian note attributes field-office closures to funding cuts; this is not evidence of conflict preventing a named climate intervention.
Protection pathway records a reported risk mechanism, not verified violence incidence or attribution of the cyclone to climate change.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
